nodes.label: One Codebase, Three Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Container stack (Phase 1), the single `lapidary` binary with agent/worker/up (Phase 4), and a Tauri desktop shell (Phase 7) — all thin shells over the same axum Router lapidary-api builds. Never fork.

nodes.label: Podman Leads, Docker Is Supported
nodes.rationale: Docker Desktop requires a paid subscription above 250 employees or $10M revenue, and government entities are excluded from the free tier at any size. The industrial and defence buyers are exactly those cases.

nodes.label: Deployment Topology
nodes.rationale: caddy web in front of axum api, Postgres beside N workers with a native OCCT sidecar, and remote workers taking leases over outbound-only HTTP.

nodes.label: Single Origin Is Mandatory
nodes.rationale: The web container reverse-proxies /api and /events to api, so there is no CORS, no cookie-domain problem and no preflight per request.

nodes.label: SSE Needs proxy_buffering off
nodes.rationale: Default buffering holds progress events until the buffer fills and ingest appears frozen. Needs the Caddy equivalent plus X-Accel-Buffering: no. Named as the single most common works-in-dev-breaks-in-prod bug in this stack.

nodes.label: Version Skew Detection
nodes.rationale: Build every image from the same commit, tag identically, expose /api/version returning the build SHA; the frontend compares against its baked-in value and shows a banner on mismatch.

nodes.label: Three Deployment Modes
nodes.rationale: Server-managed (the enterprise shape, no container runtime on workstations, sidesteps Docker Desktop licensing), local single-user via `lapidary up`, and air-gapped via podman load plus Quadlet units and an offline Ed25519 licence.

nodes.label: Twelve-Crate Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: Feature isolation enforced by the Cargo dependency graph and a CI check rather than by network boundaries: L0 core, L1 db/storage, L2 feature crates, L3 api/ingest, and an Enterprise wrapper tier.

nodes.label: CI-Enforced Layering Rule
nodes.rationale: L2 crates may depend on L0 and L1 and never on each other or on L3; anything two L2 crates need to share moves to lapidary-core. This is what keeps the monolith from congealing. Enterprise may depend on lapidary-api but never the reverse, because that edge would make the free application depend on the enterprise crate.

nodes.label: FORBIDDEN_PAIRS Named-Pair Prohibitions
nodes.rationale: lapidary-api -> lapidary-cad and lapidary-api -> lapidary-enterprise are forbidden structurally, with check_publish enforcing publish = false on every member, in xtask/src/layers.rs rather than restated in prose. edge_allowed operates on tiers and cannot express a single-pair exception, so a new prohibition extends FORBIDDEN_PAIRS.

nodes.label: lapidary-api Crate
nodes.rationale: L3 library building the axum Router for the open path, grid, health and download. Never lapidary-cad, and never lapidary-storage's SourceStore; it may name SourceReader, the read-only source handle, in download.rs and nowhere else, with cargo xtask check-deploy enforcing both halves.

nodes.label: lapidary-ingest Crate
nodes.rationale: Exists as its own crate rather than a Role::Worker check inside lapidary-api because the images are also split at build time: lapidary-api depending on lapidary-cad at all, even for a route Role::Api never mounts, makes the api image link it regardless. `cargo tree -p lapidary-server -e normal | grep lapidary-cad` is what caught that. The one crate allowed to depend on lapidary-cad and hold a SourceStore.

nodes.label: lapidary-cad Crate
nodes.rationale: L2 crate holding the Kernel trait and the OCCT sidecar driver. Linked only behind the mock-kernel Cargo feature, and only into the worker image.

nodes.label: lapidary-enterprise Crate
nodes.rationale: Licence verification, auth, RBAC, audit and the worker fleet, in a wrapper tier above L3. AGPL like the rest of the workspace — a proprietary crate linking AGPL crates would itself have to be AGPL.

nodes.label: Kernel Trait
nodes.rationale: Container-first deletes the WASM kernel variant entirely — OCCT always runs native in the worker. Keep the trait for test doubles but ship one implementation; this removed the highest-risk item in the original plan. KernelOutput = tessellation L0/L1/L2 glb, structure.json, entities.json.

nodes.label: Kernel Version Pinned Across The Fleet
nodes.rationale: Different OCCT builds produce different tessellations from identical input, and geometric diff depends on determinism. The coordinator must reject leases from workers whose kernel hash does not match the pool's pinned build, or two revisions of an unchanged part show a phantom volume delta depending on which machine processed it.

nodes.label: Why Not gRPC
nodes.rationale: ts-rs already gives typed contracts from one source; .proto would be a third schema beside SQL and Rust. Blobs must stay on plain HTTP for range requests and immutable caching, so both protocols would run anyway. protoc becomes a build dependency for every contributor, proto3 field presence blurs 'volume is 0.0' from 'volume was never computed', and tonic is not accepting significant new features. Revisit only for a second native plugin; add utoipa/OpenAPI first if a public contract is needed.

nodes.label: Supply Chain Policy
nodes.rationale: cargo-deny with a sources allow-list, not just advisories and licences — without it a transitive dependency can silently come from an arbitrary git URL. Lockfiles committed, Actions pinned to SHAs, cargo vendor for release builds because a regulated customer will ask whether you can build offline and the answer must be demonstrably yes, plus per-release SBOMs and cosign signatures.

nodes.label: No Embedded PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: There is no official embedded PostgreSQL, which is why that path was abandoned. Container mode uses the official postgres:18 Docker Official Image and the problem disappears.

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0-only For The Whole Workspace
nodes.rationale: An AGPL app plus a proprietary enterprise crate conflict: a proprietary crate linking AGPL crates must itself be AGPL, and DCO-signed contributions cannot be relicensed. Decided: everything AGPL, sell the licence contractually — the Ed25519 file gates fleet size and support as a contractual boundary, not technical DRM, and AGPL already blocks a competitor from hosting without publishing changes. A CLA was rejected for the contributor friction it would cost.

nodes.label: Pinned Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: Rust with axum/tokio/sqlx on PostgreSQL 18.6, BLAKE3 not SHA-256 because ingest is hash-bound, object_store with range reads, Postgres FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED plus LISTEN/NOTIFY instead of Redis or a broker, uuid v7 ids. Frontend is React + Vite + TypeScript with no meta-framework, TanStack Router carrying filter state in typed search params, shadcn/ui copied in rather than depended on, and CSS transitions plus the Web Animations API rather than anime.js.

hyperedges.label: The Open-Path Invariant, Enforced At Five Independent Levels
